input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: convert story points to engineering hours using a standard rule of thumb of ~6-7 hours per point per relevant role for a full-stack team (Backend + Frontend + QA + DevOps), adjusted for task nature (infra vs UI vs data migration vs integration). Total backlog points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81 points.

I allocated hours per task by role based on the nature of the work:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pts): DevOps-heavy with some Backend support.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pts): Frontend-heavy with QA for visual/regression testing.
- PW-3 (Auth, 8pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy, Frontend for UI, QA for security/regression testing.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pts): Backend-heavy (API enforcement), Frontend (UI gating), QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pts): Frontend-heavy, Backend for APIs, QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pts): Frontend + Backend (PDF gen), QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy (Stripe, webhooks, reconciliation), QA critical (money-handling), some DevOps (secrets/webhook infra).
- PW-8 (Data migration, 21pts): Backend-heavy (ETL scripts), DevOps (migration infra/cutover), QA (data validation) — no Frontend need.

Capacity check: Backend Developer 1.5 FTE ≈ 2400 hrs over a ~6 month (26 week) delivery window at 60hrs/week combined capacity (1.5 FTE * 40hrs * 26wks ≈ 1560hrs available); Frontend 1.0 FTE ≈ 1040hrs available; QA 0.6 FTE ≈ 624hrs available; DevOps 0.4 FTE ≈ 416hrs available. My allocations (Backend 700hrs, Frontend 380hrs, QA 210hrs, DevOps 130hrs) fit comfortably within these capacities for a ~4-5 month timeline, though DevOps and QA are thin relative to the number of tasks touching them (CI, payments, migration all need DevOps/QA attention) — flagged as an assumption/risk.

Non-labour costs: Stripe integration sandbox/production fees are usually transaction-based (excluded from build cost), but I included a one-time Stripe integration/compliance review fee, a staging/cloud infrastructure cost for CI pipeline, and a data migration one-time tooling/Oracle export licensing cost, plus a contingency buffer given no historical actuals exist.

Priority breakdown assigns each task's full labour+relevant non-labour cost to its priority tier.

Reductions identified: descope PW-2 design system to a minimal token-only pass now (defer full component library), reduce QA regression hours on PW-6 (lower priority, non-critical), defer PW-8 migration scope (migrate only a partial/live dataset first, backfill later), and negotiate/reduce non-labour infra spend by using existing cloud credits.
</reasoning>

nonLabourLines.description: Cloud/staging infrastructure setup and 6-month run cost (CI pipeline, staging environment)
Stripe integration setup, PCI compliance review, and webhook infra hardening (one-time)
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling / ETL licensing and export costs
Contingency buffer (no historical actuals available; ~10% of labour)

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics and task-type analysis, not past delivery data.
Story points converted to hours at a blended rate of roughly 6-7 engineering hours per point, split across roles by task nature.

Delivery horizon assumed to be approximately 4-5 months, within which current FTE capacity (1.5 Backend, 1.0 Frontend, 0.6 QA, 0.4 DevOps) is sufficient but tightly stretched, particularly for QA and DevOps given the number of tasks requiring their input (CI setup, payment integration, data migration).

DevOps Engineer at 0.4 FTE is thinly staffed relative to the combined demands of CI/staging setup, payment webhook infra, and migration cutover support; this is a schedule risk even though total hours fit within nominal capacity.

QA Engineer at 0.6 FTE is similarly thin given testing needs across auth, payments, RBAC, and migration validation; QA hours were prioritized toward Urgent/High tasks (auth, payments, RBAC) at the expense of lower-priority items.
Stripe transaction fees themselves are excluded from this estimate as they are ongoing operational costs, not one-time build costs; only integration/setup effort is included.
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumes a single migration pass with validation; does not include extended parallel-run/dual-write reconciliation period, which would add cost if required.
Design system (PW-2) is scoped as a working component library sufficient for the other UI tasks, not a fully polished, documented design system.
Rate card figures and FTE availability provided are treated as fixed and accurate for the estimate period.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 Design System to a minimal token + core component set now, deferring advanced components (tables, dialogs theming polish) to a later phase
reductions.effect: Reduces Frontend and QA hours on PW-2 by roughly half

reductions.description: Reduce QA regression depth on PW-6 (Invoice list/detail), a Medium-priority, lower-risk feature, relying on automated smoke tests instead of full manual regression
reductions.effect: Cuts QA hours allocated to PW-6 by ~40 hours

reductions.description: Phase PW-8 Legacy Data Migration: migrate active/recent customer records and invoices first, defer historical archive migration to a follow-on project
reductions.effect: Reduces Backend and DevOps migration hours by roughly a third and cuts migration tooling licensing cost

reductions.description: Use existing cloud provider credits/reserved capacity instead of new staging infrastructure spend for PW-1
Defer full PCI compliance review to post-launch audit, doing a lighter internal checklist now for PW-7 initial release
reductions.effect: Reduces one-time Stripe integration/compliance non-labour cost
